name: base64::decode::decode_engine
evidence: Proof.lean: deng_refines (Old = ok r -> New = ok (resMap r)); deng_old_overflow (as_ref input = ok s, usize::MAX < s.len*4 -> Old = fail integerOverflow); deng_rel (exact relation: Old ;map resMap = as_ref; len*4; /3; New); all kernel-checked, no sorry
hypotheses: hmap : New.core.result.Result.map inst (resMap r) f = Old.core.result.Result.map inst r f >>= ok o resMap (same external generic fn Result::map, instantiated at the two Aeneas copies of DecodeError; i.e. it commutes with the copy isomorphism)

Engine impl correspondence: New impl = engMap instO (field-wise copy; decode output's DecodeError mapped by errMap). engMap is a bijection so all corresponding impl pairs are covered. AsRef impl, E, T, Config, DecodeEstimate types are shared.
notes: Aeneas does not model Vec capacity: alloc.vec.Vec.with_capacity _ n := Vec.new, so the capacity change itself (the only real difference: capacity of the returned Vec) is invisible in the model. However the old code still evaluates input.as_ref().len() * 4 with overflow checking (Aeneas = debug-build semantics) and panics when len*4 > usize::MAX (possible for slices of length in (usize::MAX/4, isize::MAX], e.g. >1 GiB inputs on 32-bit targets, debug builds only); the new code never computes it. Hence REFINES in the model (new more defined); in release builds (wrapping arithmetic) the two are EQUIV. 'Not conversely' is witnessed only on the old side (old = fail integerOverflow); whether new returns ok there depends on the user Engine impl and opaque Vec::as_mut_slice. Old also calls as_ref twice (once for the capacity hint, once in decode_engine_vec); the model treats AsRef::as_ref as a pure function, so this is harmless. Proof time ~20 min.

name: base64::decode::decode_engine
precondition: for every s with input.as_ref() = Ok(s): s.len() * 4 <= usize::MAX (no overflow in the old capacity hint; not a documented library guarantee, but holds for every input that fits in memory on 64-bit targets)
